## About
Champion Septic Tank is a family-owned business that takes care of septic tanks, grease traps, lift stations and storm drains for homes and businesses across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties. We treat every customer with respect and work to get each job done right the first time.
Our crews use high-powered vacuum trucks, camera inspection tools and hydro jetting equipment. Restaurants call us for grease trap cleaning and used cooking oil pickup, and homeowners call us to find, pump and clean their tanks.
We answer the phone day or night and speak English and Spanish. Our neighbors have given us a 5-star rating across 208 Google reviews.

## Services
- Septic Tank Pumping & Cleaning: High-powered vacuum trucks and modern cleaning equipment to remove sludge, scum and buildup, for homes and commercial properties.
- Grease Trap Cleaning: We remove accumulated grease, fats and oils, clean the trap thoroughly, dispose of it properly and help you stay in line with local regulations.
- Used Cooking Oil Collection: Pickup for restaurants, commercial kitchens, hotels, supermarkets, cafeterias, ghost kitchens, catering companies and food trucks across Miami-Dade and Broward.
- Lift Station Maintenance: Pump inspections, cleaning and repairs that catch problems early and keep your wastewater system running.
- Storm Drain Services: Cleaning, maintenance and repairs that keep drains clear of debris, so your property stays safe and dry during heavy rains.
- Hydro Jetting: High-pressure water jets clear out debris, grease, tree roots and stubborn clogs that traditional methods can't handle.
- Sewer Camera Inspection: A camera look inside your pipes and septic system to find blockages, leaks and other issues before we fix them.
- Flood Emergency Pump-Outs: 24/7 emergency pump-outs with powerful equipment to remove standing water and protect your property from damage.

## FAQ
Q: How often should I have my septic tank pumped?
A: The recommendation is every 2-3 years, depending on the size of your tank and how much water your household uses. We can look at your system and give you a recommendation for your situation.

Q: Is septic pumping the same as septic cleaning?
A: Not quite. Pumping removes the liquid and some solid waste. Cleaning is more thorough and removes all the sludge and scum buildup.

Q: How do I know my septic system needs attention?
A: Watch for slow drains, gurgling sounds in the plumbing, bad odors around the tank or drainfield, standing water or wet spots in the yard, and sewage backups in the house.

Q: What do you offer for commercial properties?
A: Septic tank pumping, grease trap maintenance and pumping, lift station cleaning and repairs, hydro jetting and storm drain maintenance, so your business keeps running.
